paper_role: independent reproductive-performance validation of history-dependent colony redistribution

motivation.problem: The earlier chick-production state uses a breeding-pair denominator that can overlap conceptually with colony abundance. REPRO provides nest-level reproductive histories whose primary success endpoint does not use the colony census as a denominator.
motivation.question: Does independently measured nest reproductive success in season t predict where Adelie breeders accumulate by the next breeding census?

row_identity_and_fail_closed_rules.season: Parse studyName with the already frozen PALYYZZ season rule used for Palmer chick data.
row_identity_and_fail_closed_rules.duplicates: If a nest key appears more than once, exclude every row belonging to that duplicated key; do not average or select records.
row_identity_and_fail_closed_rules.colony_match: Exact archived Colony string match to the adult census after only whitespace stripping; no aggregation of colony codes.

nest_success_endpoint.creched_chicks: Count 1 for each of Chick 1 Creche Date and Chick 2 Creche Date that contains a non-empty, non-missing recorded value; allowed range 0-2.
nest_success_endpoint.colony_season_success: mean creched_chicks across eligible monitored nests within raw Island + Colony + season
nest_success_endpoint.reason: Reduce domination by very small monitored samples while retaining a directly interpretable chicks-to-creche-per-monitored-nest quantity.

performance_state.eligibility: Within an island-season, require at least 3 colony codes with >=5 monitored nests and finite colony-season success.
performance_state.standardization: z-standardize colony_season_success across eligible colonies within each island-season; call this R_i,t.
performance_state.sampling_weight: Primary model is unweighted so each eligible colony-season is one unit. Report monitored-nest counts descriptively.
performance_state.interpretation: R_i,t is relative nest reproductive success independent of the adult-census abundance denominator.

redistribution_outcome.growth: G_i,t = log1p(adult_pairs_i,t+1) - log1p(adult_pairs_i,t) for adjacent annual censuses only.
redistribution_outcome.relative_growth: Within island and transition t -> t+1, subtract the mean G across eligible matched colony codes.
redistribution_outcome.prior_size_control: Within the matched island-transition set, z-standardize log1p(adult_pairs_i,t).
redistribution_outcome.rationale: Because R_i,t is nest-based and does not contain adult_pairs_i,t, lag 1 is the primary temporally aligned endpoint without the earlier shared-denominator concern.

primary_model.formula: relative_growth_i,t = beta_1 * R_i,t + gamma * z_log_size_i,t + island:colony fixed effect + error

inference.null: Within each predictor island-season, colony labels of R_i,t are exchangeable with respect to next-year redistribution conditional on prior size and colony identity.
inference.permutation: Permute R_i,t among all eligible colonies within predictor island-season; preserve outcome, missingness and controls.
inference.p_value: one-sided upper-tail Monte Carlo p with +1 correction

secondary_lag2.formula: Same model but outcome is relative growth during t+1 -> t+2, with z_log_size measured at t+1.
secondary_lag2.role: Temporal persistence check comparable to the earlier chick-production lag-2 result; not required for the primary decision.

minimum_information_gate.failure: If any minimum is not met, STOP without fitting the performance-growth coefficient or running permutation inference.

sensitivities.minimum_nests_10: Repeat primary after requiring >=10 monitored nests per colony-season.
sensitivities.binary_any_creche: Repeat using proportion of monitored nests with >=1 creched chick, standardized within island-season.
sensitivities.exclude_litchfield: Repeat primary excluding LIT if LIT is represented.
sensitivities.leave_one_island_out: Report observed primary beta after excluding each represented island in turn.
sensitivities.leave_one_colony_out: Report observed primary beta after excluding each colony when the minimum-information gate remains satisfied.

convergent_validity_secondary.question: Does nest-level R_i,t align with the previously frozen chick-production performance state S_i,t where both exist?
convergent_validity_secondary.statistic: Pearson correlation after within-island-season centering is already built into both standardized states.
convergent_validity_secondary.role: Descriptive only; it does not change the primary decision.

decision_rule.support: Primary beta_1 > 0 and one-sided permutation p <= 0.05.
decision_rule.failure: Otherwise do not claim independent nest-level validation of performance-linked redistribution.
decision_rule.strong_replication: Primary support plus positive beta_1 under minimum_nests_10 and binary_any_creche sensitivities.

claim_boundaries: A positive result would independently validate a performance-to-redistribution association, not prove public-information use or individual movement.
Do not change the creche endpoint, five-nest threshold, lag, controls, alpha, or permutation rule after REPRO outcome values are opened.
Do not infer predation, snow, or habitat quality from REPRO alone.
If the minimum-information gate fails, do not lower it or substitute another reproductive endpoint post hoc.
